file.content:
OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

content.text:
The build is green. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Change

`POST /api/owners` now rejects a request that is missing or blank in any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, or `telephone`, responding **400** with a JSON body `{"errors": [...]}` naming each offending field.

Following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions (not Spring MVC), I added a validation step to the front of the pipeline plus a matching escalation handler:

**New files**
- `rest/function/owner/ValidateOwnerFields.java` — first step in the pipeline. Binds `@RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto`, checks the five fields for null/blank, throws `OwnerFieldsValidationException` listing the bad field names, or republishes the body as `Out<OwnerFieldsDto>` when valid.
- `rest/escalation/OwnerFieldsValidationException.java` — checked exception carrying the field-name list.
- `rest/escalation/OwnerFieldsValidationExceptionHandler.java` — responds `400` with `{"errors": [...]}`.
- `officefloor/escalation/...OwnerFieldsValidationException.yml` — wires the handler.

**Edited files**
- `officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` — added the `validate` step ahead of `build`.
- `rest/function/owner/BuildOwner.java` — now consumes the validated body via `@Val OwnerFieldsDto` instead of re-binding `@RequestBody` (the HTTP body may only be bound once per pipeline).

**Tests:** full suite green — `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`, including the missing-city (asserts `$.errors` contains `"city"`), blank-telephone, and complete-owner cases.
